sentences.text: Palaeorhincodon is an extinct genus of prehistoric whale sharks.
Its teeth were very small, measuring only 3 millimeters in height, yet each jaw contained up to 300 rows of them.
The animal possessed an immense number of tiny teeth, with up to 300 rows packed into a single jaw.
Fossils of these creatures have been found in warm water areas spanning North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa.
Paleontologist Jacques Herman described the genus Palaeorhincodon and its type species P. wardi in 1974.
A new species, P. daouii, was named in 1997.
Researchers suggest it fed on plankton and larger pelagic animals such as small crustaceans, fish, and squid.
The genus currently includes three known species, belonging to the class Chondrichthyes and the parent group Rhinocodontidae.
The genus existed from the Aalenian to the Tortonian, between 174.7 and 7.246 million years ago.
